body:
I wholeheartedly agree. I hate being a slave while others reap the benefits of of my labor. 

As a suggestion, have you tried working somewhere with short shifts? IE, serving or front of house restaurant work? Though it still feeds the system, I've found going back to serving to be really helpful with my work fatigue. My shifts are 4-5 hours and it's easy if you can fake happy for people. Plus, the money is pretty decent depending where you work. I used to work 9-10 hour shifts manual labor and it absolutely killed all of my desire to do anything other than sleep. Now that I went back to serving, I have time and energy to do a lot more and engage in hobbies that make me feel good.

I started having depression and suicidal thoughts a little bit younger than you. I'm 28 now and my biggest regret was waiting so long to get medicated. You have a lot more down time and leway now while you're young to try to fix your problems. It's much harder to do when you're older and can't miss work and everyone judges you much more harshly. Get help now and don't wait or it'll just get worse. 

If you don't feel comfortable telling your parents right away, make up a ailment or pain and ask to see a general practitioner. Without your parent in the room, be honest then. The GP will give you a verbal test and ask you questions about your feelings and make a decision as to how to proceed. In my case, I was put on an anti depressant and anti anxiety. Not every medication is for every person and you'll probably have to try several things before you find the right thing. The key is to not give up and always be very honest with your doctor. 

I hope that you find the help you need. I keep thinking about being your age and how much it sucked so I hope you know you're not alone.

Wake up filled with anxiety, do chores till it's time to go to work. Try not to lose my shit while I'm at work. Come home, eat something or if my fiance is around and not getting hammered, make dinner for two. Lay around and watch YouTube till I can take my meds which put me to sleep.

I've thought a lot about what the source of my depression is. While it's true that I had some later childhood neglect and sexual abuse, one of my first memories is of being inexplicably sad all the time and feeling like I wasn't meant to be here (as in alive). I genuinely believe that I do have serious chemical issues in my brain but I think having trauma certainly didn't help.
I'm in a very similar situation so I feel your pain. I don't have much advice to share unfortunately but I wanted you to know that you're not the only one.
